Great food court with a lively campus atmosphere!

A nice place to enjoy a meal at NTU, especially if you are looking for variety. There are many different food stalls and choices, including local Asian food, Indian, Western dishes, snacks, desserts, drinks and more. NTU is known for having a wide range of food options across its campus.

The food court has a spacious and colourful atmosphere, with plenty of seating and large glass windows that bring in natural light and greenery from outside. The open layout makes it a comfortable place to have lunch, meet friends, or simply relax after walking around the campus.

I especially liked the bright and cheerful interior design, with different seating areas and plenty of food choices in one place. It can get quite lively during busy periods, which adds to the university atmosphere.

review_text:
A Hot Hideout at Junction 10 has become my go-to "secret hideout" whenever I need good food and some quiet me-time. Today, I visited their NTU branch for the first time, and I am thrilled to report that the food quality is just as good here!

I ordered my usual Mala Stir Fry. The texture of the noodles was perfectly springy, and the seasoning was deeply flavourful, carrying that familiar, well-balanced mala kick without being overly numbing. The bowl was loaded with fresh ingredients, including tender pork slices, sweet potato starch sheets etc. and a generous heap of fresh coriander and peanuts. We also paired it with a side of fried luncheon meat and fried otah cheese.

The campus stall has a comfortable, clean setting, and the kitchen team prepares everything with great care. It is wonderful to know I can get the exact same customisable flavours closer to this side of Singapore. Definitely an easy 5 stars!

The lotus root chips are my absolute favourite, and the fried items are placed in a separate bowl so they remain crispy, which is a nice touch.

Pricing is generally reasonable as most items are charged at a flat rate regardless of what you pick. However, do take note that if you plan to order the lotus root and potato chips, they are calculated by weight and can add up quite a bit to the total bill.

For spicy lovers, their medium spicy is already quite hot for me. My colleague ordered the max spicy level, and that was seriously fiery.

Overall, the food tastes great and I would highly recommend it!

review_text:
TGIF! Lunch at A Hot Hideout @ NTU - Mala hotpot!

My colleagues jio-ed me for lunch at this popular mala hotpot spot in NTU campus. It's a short walk from the canteen and was already packed when we arrived--we waited about 10 minutes for an outdoor table.

We tried the fried lotus root and fried potato slices, and my tip is to enjoy them immediately while they're hot and crispy. Once they cool down, they lose a bit of that "WOW" factor.

The mala here is nicely localized to suit Singaporean tastes--flavorful, fragrant, and not overly numbing. What really surprised me was the scrambled egg topping up on the Mala hotpot and "Green Tarik drink". Highly recommended! The refreshing drink paired perfectly with the spicy mala, making every bite extra shiok.

Great food, good company, and a satisfying way to kick off the weekend. No wonder this place is always crowded!

I have reported this incident to SFA as well as the outlet. So far, SFA has responded, but I have not received any response from the outlet itself.

Name: A Hot Hideout
name: KB Chong
review_text:
Overall 7 /10.

If u include the soup base of $2.50, based on 337g, it cost $4 per 100g which is pricier than yangguofu and Zhang Liang.
The taste of the soup is not as tasty as YGF and Zhang Liang. But maybe it is more healthy and sinful. If it is really so, can explain in a poster so we know the lack of taste is indeed compensated by healthier ingredients.

The deep fried lotus roots is quite new concept but not well implemented as it is not crispy.

The parking is also more expensive than most malls and downtown @> $2.40 per hour.

The loud music likely is meant for noisy lunch crowd. But today is quite a quiet afternoon since it is Dec 30.

Should pay more attention to small flies. Spotted them on the vegetables near the top shelf. I did avoid those vegetables.

The staff were quite friendly and very very united. Saw them having a nice meal together. Like this homely spirit between the staff.
response_from_owner_text:
Hi there. Thank you for taking the time to share such detailed feedback! We really appreciate your honest observations.

We'll review the pricing and taste of our soup, and your suggestion about highlighting the health benefits on a poster is excellent, we'll look into making that clearer.

We also appreciate your notes on the deep-fried lotus root and will work on improving its crispiness. Regarding parking, music, and hygiene, your points are well-taken, and we'll strive to improve the overall environment for our guests.

We're glad you noticed our team spirit, our staff truly enjoy working together, and it means a lot that it shows. We hope to welcome you back soon with an even better experience!

review_translated_text:
The staff are friendly.

It's all about whole potatoes and lotus root.

I was curious how they do it, but if you don't select "not fried" when ordering, they fry it and put it on top as a topping.

I ordered Xiang Guo; I wonder if they would put the Mala Tang on top of that too.

They said it was super delicious?? It's not bad, but it has absolutely no umami flavor.

It's all about whole potatoes and lotus root.

If you come to Korea, try Hei Mao Cai.

It's on the expensive side. The whole potatoes and lotus roots are big and heavy; it came out to over 20 dollars.

I don't recommend the bamboo shoots or the purple rice cake (I thought it was sweet potato, but it's cheese?); it smells really bad.

The cheese fish cake is tasty, but the cheese is a bit salty.

The quail eggs have absolutely no nutty flavor.

You should probably just take a little bit, focusing on fish cakes and shrimp.

The sauce isn't great, so even if the fried tofu soaks up the sauce, it's not that great.

The mushrooms are in poor condition, and it's too expensive for the taste.

So, come with two people, take a little bit, and just try the lotus root and potatoes.

name: Eileen Neo (Sgsohotleh)
review_text:
This place has been getting a lot of hype recently on Instagram and TikTok. Ordered the Mala Collagen Soup (Xiao La)--it was surprisingly drinkable and flavorful!

USP is that they fry some of the ingredients like fish, potato, and lotus. But it's heavy and they charged by the weight. So imagine getting your eggs, lotus and potato. Heavier than meat However, I probably wouldn't reorder the fried items as they were quite dry and oily, with no seasoning or marination. We ended up dipping the fried items into our Mala soup.

Ingredients were fresh, but there were a lot of flies around the sauce station, where you help yourself to peanuts, spring onions, and their "secret powder."

Would say it's a decent experience, will still visit to try other soup base.

name: Nathan
review_text: I went here with my friends to get the stir fried mala. Their unique selling point as compared to other mala stalls is the deep fried toppings, which includes lotus roots, fried luncheon meat, and scrambled eggs. I definitely recommend getting the deep fried toppings since you cannot get these kinds of toppings in any other mala stalls (at least not that I have found). They also sell thai milk tea here which I also recommend buying. Prior to this visit, I went here once to try the scrambled eggs, but I do not really like it as I felt the flavor of the egg diluted the mala flavor. The mala itself is pretty good (I'd say above average) with a moderately strong flavor and not too much oil. However, I felt the flavor profile was a bit lacking as compared to another mala place that I frequented. Also, this place is a bit pricier than the typical mala stalls you will find in food courts. Even so, I still feel Hot Hideout's mala is above average, and if you are an NTU student or in NTU's vicinity, I definitely recommend going here to eat at least once.

response_from_owner_text:
Hi Tanya, sincere apologies that the aircon was turned off earlier than the stated closing time. We have looked into the matter and trained the staffs accordingly.
As for the mala soup, we have checked that the last portion of soup was served ard 8:40pm for the order taken at 8:20pm. Do note that our last order is 9pm - when soup runs out at 8:20pm, we cannot have the kitchen to cook the whole pot of soup as it takes time and will cause food wastage since we throw all leftover soup on the same day.
For the milk tea, our staff is trained not to serve milk tea which are freshly brewed. It is a crucial part of our recipe that we have to cool the brewed tea for a certain period before serving. The milk tea at you are seeing on the counter are those that are freshly brewed, left to cool down before we chilled it. We have trial and tested that if we just served the hot tea with ice, the drink will not taste as good. Please understand that we do not compromise quality of the drinks customers are receiving in return for higher sales.
For the salty feedback, we can suggest that customers can select the "less salt" option if they are customers who prefer less salty. Thank you.

Name: A Hot Hideout
name: Snehal
review_text:
There was this unknown white thing in our food that we hadn't added to our hotpot bowl. We couldn't even recognise it, turns out its a boiled egg, it was really upsetting because it had been cooked in the same bowl along with the rest of our food and we strictly don't eat egg. What if next time we find meat in our food? What if next time we find something that we are allergic to in our bowl?
It is not about the egg, it is about how the egg leads us to lose trust in this restaurant.
We removed the egg to the side but honestly after seeing it I totally lost my appetite. We actually asked the lady what it is, and she just stammered something, looked away and left our table. Didn't even give us a clear response. They can't even accept their mistake.
The point of hotpot is to be able to customize your bowl. I have had experiences with other restaurants where they do cook food with egg, or add fish sauce etc but I can understand that because I am not customizing the dish myself and I understand that I should clarify before I order. But with hotpot random ingredients should never float into my bowl.
Also, there are a lot of reviews here saying they found missing ingredients in their cooked bowl. SO I am guessing those ingredients made their way into other bowls. Maybe someone missed an egg in their bowl last sunday?

Name: A Hot Hideout
name: Y Lai
review_text:
After watching the review of a food vlogger we decided to try.

They go by weight and it's not the cheapest. If you want to really get your money's worth, just take all meat, seafood and mushroom. Forget anything green.

None of the food is labelled so, choosing the meat is just a matter of fatty or lean.

They are very responsive on the telegram chat so just check with them for any queries.

Ideally, start your meal no later than 6.30 pm. The queue gets out of control towards the night. We stepped in at 6pm and we were eating in less than 15 minutes.

The spice level of "low" is equal to "Wei la" outside.

The fried potato, is no different from potato chips, nothing really amazing, maybe potato chips are cheaper.

The fried lotus root was interesting. Since we do not find the fried lotus root chips outside easily, it is worth a return trip. Our nitpick is, they just fry the items without seasoning, no Cajun powder no salt n pepper. (OK maybe the dory had salt) perhaps my expectation were shaped by LokLok and therefore too high.

I would really have preferred if they deep fried then somehow integrated the mala sauce with the fried items, maybe offer a dip. Maybe I am too influenced by loklok.

The scrambled eggs are just scrambled eggs without any seasoning.

Every other item was typical of a Mala shop. Either you agree with the taste or disagree. I agree with the taste.

The green and brown drink is Thai milk tea. The green one seems to be Thai milk tea with jasmine green tea. They are not really strong brew, but worth the $2.50 price tag. Probably one of the cheapest Thai milk tea.

There is a strange smell on the tray, but small matter, just put it away.

Unlike many other eating places in NTU there is no student price for flashing your student card here.

This place is not worth a detour. It is worth trying if you are in the area or you drive.

All ingredients($1.99/100g)
Mala Dry($1.50)
Mala Collagen Soup($2.50)
Add rice/noodles($0.80)
I had Medium Spicy Collagen Soup with Noodles at a total of $11.85.
Soup is rich and comforting but is a tad salty. The collagen is said to be cooked over 12 hours. Yes, you can taste the moderate collagenness & creaminess in the watery soup but I prefer it to be more thicker then can enjoy the full richness to the maximum. Oil level is appropriate, spicy level is not that spicy for me, numbness had a higher ratio I feel. Still a pretty tastisfying soup.
As for some ingredients like fish, I like how they fried them to retain some texture and give a light crisp to it before adding to soup. I took meat, mushroom and vegetables too. More importantly, I spam more prawn and fish. Finally, soup are garnished with minced garlic and coriander.

Great place to chill too.

I didn't know there was a Western restaurant with such a nice atmosphere on campus.

The lunch set is incredibly good value. It includes a large steak, a soup, dessert, and a pot of tea, and even with tax and service, it only comes to $40.

If you have a long break between classes and nothing else to do, this is a great place to spend some time eating steak and drinking tea. The atmosphere is quiet and not too crowded, so it's okay to stop by without a reservation.

However, I recommend lowering your expectations for the food. Honestly, the steak I ordered medium-rare was a bit tough, almost like chewing rubber. Still, considering the price, I can't expect too much, and overall, I think it's a decent choice for the price.

name: Soh Hwa Goh
review_text:
Pictures on Food poster and menu at NTUAC showed complimentary soup and dessert brownie at $8 each with each main dish order. But actual serve was soup without garlic bread and brownie without ice cream. What you see is not what you get. False advertising was used here.

Next, mind you to check that service charge and GST are applied on the complimentary soup and dessert. Manager Rajiv explained that the food needed to be brought to the table and that was service rendered. But all other restaurants that I patronized don't charge service charge and GST for 50% off Hi-tea or 1-1 deals. Good job to all these restaurants.

The poster indicated $8++ on the complimentary items. Hence, it was consistent with their billing calculations.

Next round when I was at NTUAC, the $8++ on the soup and dessert were strike off.

Last I was there, no more such poster displayed.

Just note that so far only Pen&Inc and Cali restaurants make such practices.

Recently, manager Rajiv had poor customer service attitudes. He could make your pleasant dining experience a shock when billing came. I used two birthday vouchers and had a less than $1 balance on my first order. Then I ordered a beverage and I was issued two receipts for one seating. I had to ask for the first receipt after I was given the second receipt paid for cappuccino. Usually, one seating one bill and a final bill made with whatever balance you have to offset. Rajiv was happy not to amend the first bill and not transfer the balance to the second bill. He was adamant not to do anything and claimed that I asked for billing when I gave the waiter the vouchers.

Finally, the lesson learnt is best don't patronise Pen&Inc and Cali so you don't have the bad experience after a meal.

Meanwhile, two other staff stood by doing nothing and made no effort to help. The lack of basic courtesy and professionalism was unacceptable.

I can't help but wonder if we were treated this poorly simply because we are students.

I urge management to take this matter seriously.

Name: PEN & INC
name: Ruth May Bunda
review_text:
Pen and Inc.

A sports bar cafe and restaurant situated near one-North MRT. When we visited the place is so quiet

We ordered calamari for appetizer, it was quite okay, the squid was just overcooked but the fry is golden to perfection.

The wagyu cheeseburger is a must! Very meaty and juicy, the meat was thick also! We liked the fries for the side.

For the pan seared salmon, you cannot go wrong with salmon. Cooked with freshness and the tangy lemon flavor compliments it more. The mash potato was so smooth but quite bland; but still manage to go well with the salmon.

For the pasta, there's a taste of burn garlic but the creaminess and the amount of serving is good.

All in all, we enjoyed our time together, we step out of the cafe feeling full and satisfied. Plus points we had a great time playing billiards and darts!
A place to eat and play and hang out together with your friends

Name: PEN & INC
name: C'estLaVie
review_text:
After discovering PEN & INC through Google reviews, we decided to visit the restaurant located in NTU. Following the signage and direction boards, we easily located the establishment. Our visit took place on a weekend late afternoon, and we were among only three patrons at that time.
We thoroughly enjoyed the restaurant's vibe and the background music. Our order included the Slow Cooked Beef Cheek, Fish & Chips, Honey Mustard Chicken Leg, Meat Beef Ragu Pasta, and the highly recommended Lava Torte for dessert. All dishes were impeccably prepared, with each item reaching the perfect level of tenderness and harmonizing well with its respective sauces. It's challenging to pinpoint a single "Must Try" item, as every dish was truly worth sampling.

Among our favorites was the Chocolate Baked Lava Cake, exuding a delightful fragrance of chocolate and mild milk. Served piping hot and paired with cold vanilla ice cream, each bite resulted in a satisfying melding of flavors that melted in our mouths.

The waitstaff and entire crew were not only friendly but also deserving of a double thumbs up for their excellent service. Our visit to Pen & INC proved to be a delightful and memorable experience, making for a wonderful afternoon.

Please ascertain the facts before making sweeping statements like 'Don't bother coming, they are likely closed". review_text:
This place is located at the heart of NTU in Northspine! (Near the KFC). I was decently surprised by the ambience! It was cosy and comforting.

I ordered the beef cheeks, pork loin fajita, wagyu burger and lava cake.

The Wagyu burger was disappointing. It cost a whopping 18 dollars! However, the patty was really bland. There was no seasoning at all. I had to add my own pepper and salt to the patty to make it tasty. The onions were raw and not grilled. However, I have to say that the fries were good! ($18)

Next, the beef cheeks were soft and tender to the bone. Sauce was decent and mash potato is creamy! However, there's not enough sauce to pair with the mash potato as it was paired with the beef cheeks. (Preferred the fries). They could have been more generous with the salad portion. Overall a bit too pricey for this dish. ($22)

Lastly, the pork loin fajita was surprisingly good!! Pork was cooked and seasoned well! It was paired with onions which was good as well! The combination with the wrap and the pork was really delicious. It even came with a side of sour cream and guacamole! Overall a really really good dish that I recommend :)) It was the cheapest out of the 3 main dish. ($16)

When dessert came, I was pleasantly surprised on the presentation of the dish. The lava cake came off a bit sweet but paired really well with the vanilla ice cream. (Although they probably used a cheap ice cream brand) A great way to end the meal :) ($6)

Overall, dish place is a must try if you have the money as it comes off a little pricey. Would recommend if you are finding a place to splurge. Till we meet again, au revoir!

name: Shi Ting Lim
review_text:
Quite disappointed with the service at the drinks and fried snacks stall. The staff are not rude, but they seem to have a habit of selectively ignoring certain requests. On multiple occasions, I've clearly asked for sweet and savoury items to be packed separately. The first time, I assumed it might have been a misunderstanding, but it has happened repeatedly since then.

Despite making the same request each time, the staff continue to pack everything together without acknowledging it. If separate packing is not allowed, it would be more professional to inform customers upfront rather than simply ignoring the request and proceeding anyway.

This is especially inconvenient when I'm buying breakfast for colleagues and need items to be packed separately. I hope the stall can improve on communication and pay more attention to customers' requests.

review_translated_text:
After being amazed by the large braised pork pot (the spicy and Liuzhou flavors are good) and spicy hot pot (the spicy flavor should be low in oil and salt) at Taiwai Cuisine, I was then blown away by the "large intestine wrapped in small intestine"! Although the salt and pepper chicken was just okay, the eggplant bento looked great, although I don't like overly sweet or heavy soy sauce flavors.

After a period of not knowing what to eat every day, I discovered the newly opened Vietnamese window, and in 2025 I fell in love with Canteen A again!

The beef and pork rice noodles had a wide variety of delicious meats; I felt like I wanted more after finishing them. Remember to add lime juice and chopped chili to the soup noodles! Otherwise, you'll miss the essence.

The various meat sandwiches also look worth trying!

I'm alive again!

Day 2: Today I had pig tail rice noodles and grilled meat spring rolls. The spring rolls even had crispy bits inside! It's incredible!

I'm adding a highly recommended dish : the large braised pot. The old man who sells noodles moved across the street to make room for this place. It's spicy, but the numbing sensation is incredible. The fragrant and spicy flavor is just average. I tried the spicy pork trotter and beef tendon noodles, and my mouth waters every day afterward Be prepared that the lady taking my order will have oily hands, but I didn't mind at all because it's so delicious.

review_translated_text:
The herbal Bak Kut Teh is pretty good; the braised noodles and prawn noodles are decent.

The pork rib soup is good.

The dried beef kway teow at the Vietnamese Cuisine restaurant in the other small hall is delicious, served with beef soup.

The dry beef kway teow is very delicious, has a unique exotic feel, a large quantity of beef, and plenty of sauce at the bottom of the bowl, sided with beef soup--just $5. You can add extra sauce (reddish, slightly spicy, very special) yourself.

The owner closed for a while because a child was sick, but it's reopened now. They give a lot of beef slices. Not many people try it, but I'll still give it a try.

name: Dennis Yeo
review_text:
This is the worst Popeyes outlet in the west!

I ordered a bucket of spicy chicken meal from the self-service kiosk at around 1:00 PM and took a seat to wait. After 30 minutes, my food still wasn't ready so I went to the counter to check. The staff told me they were still preparing the spicy chicken and asked me to wait a little longer, so I had no choice but to continue waiting.

By 1:50 PM, I had already been waiting for 50 minutes and was running out of patience. I went back to the counter again, only to be told that the spicy chicken still wasn't ready. They then asked if I wanted to switch to the non-spicy chicken, even though there was already a whole tray of it available.

I asked them how it could possibly take more than 50 minutes to prepare a bucket of chicken. I only have a one-hour lunch break and I ended up wasting almost the entire break waiting for food that never arrived.

If there was going to be such a long wait, why wasn't I informed earlier or given the option to switch to non-spicy chicken from the start? Better communication would have saved both my time and frustration.

How is this considered fast food when customers have to wait nearly an hour for a simple order? Extremely disappointing service..

review_text:
Terrible experience at Popeyes NTU
I waited nearly 30 minutes for my order, only to watch a staff member try to hand me food from a cancelled delivery order that had been sitting out for almost an hour and was already going cold. I refused it.

She then claimed they were out of spicy chicken -- despite me having ordered three pieces of spicy. When I asked why they couldn't just cook a fresh batch, she told me I'd have to wait another 15 minutes.

Here's the dishonest part: while I waited, I watched her take the same rejected, hour-old food I had just refused and slip it into the orders of two or three customers who came in after me -- including two cups of soda that had been sitting out and were almost certainly flat. Those customers had no idea.

Serving stale food to unsuspecting customers isn't just lazy, it's dishonest and a food safety issue. Won't be coming back.

Name: Popeyes
name: Apple juice
review_text:
I'd like to share about a bad experience with a particular worker from Popeyes. On 15 April 2026 at around 8pm, my friends and I had just finished ordering our food and were looking for seats. We were going to sit in a corner with a sign that said "caution wet floor." It should be noted that there was a worker mopping the floor at this point, and by then the restaurant was pretty empty, so it was not clear to us that this was an out-of-bounds area for customers.

As we were approaching the corner, we heard a voice yell "oi you think this your grandfather restaurant ah?" It was the worker mopping the floor. It was an incredibly rude jolt to us.

I want to point out that we fully understand why certain areas may be out-of-bounds to customers, and we were more than willing to comply with whatever requests that were being made, as we did by sitting in another area of the restaurant. We have absolutelh no issue with this, but the problem was how this worker was speaking (or more aptly put, yelling) at us. He is someone who works in customer service, and no matter how frustrated the day may have been, he should have had some manners. And this is coming from a person who has worked in customer service for an extended period of time and has faced many frustrations at work. There was absolutely no reason for him to be acting this way towards us.

To add on, I am not sure if this was a mere coincidence or if it was done with intent, but as I was walking back to our table after collecting our food, he slammed his wet mop quite near to my feet.

His description: skinny, average height, bespectacled

name: Samantha
review_text:
Horrible outlet with rude staff. Very disorganised. The queue numbers on the screen are only there for show.

I ordered my food, stood in front of the counter, and watched the staff preparing lots of mobile orders. I saw my order number under "Now Preparing" on the queue screen so I waited. Then it disappeared. It was not under "Serving", and no one had called my number (which I do not even understand since isn't the point of the screen is so no numbers need to be called)?

So I approached this male staff at the counter and asked if my order was ready since the number was not on the screen. He glanced at my receipt and said rudely and sarcastically, "Ma'am please wait it has only been 3 minutes". Even had the cheek to glare. I tried telling him that I ONLY asked because my number had disappeared from the screen and he replied loudly and impatiently, "I will call the number when it is ready" - as if I am supposed to be familiar with their messed up system. So much for the screen alert advising you to "Please watch here for your number".

The patty on the cheeseburger was too salty, and the ice in my drink was already half melted.

Based on the reviews I've seen here, McDonald's should do something about the staff and system at this outlet.

Name: McDonald's
name: Andre Khoo (ANK55)
review_text:
Advice for those who want fast orders from this place:

Just do Pick Up orders, for some reason they just like to prioritize orders that are pick up rather than dine in options.

Also don't do any coupon redemptions from this place. They like to always push those orders to the back of the queue. And they also like to screw up the coupon redemption orders as well.

Unless you want to wait for 1+ hours (legit if I haven't asked for a refund I would probably be waiting till lunch hours), just follow these steps.

Or do mobile orders, they sure love to do mobile orders as there are always 10+ mobile orders done already but left on the counter for like 30+ mins.

Name: McDonald's
name: wesley lim
review_text:
Ordered a dine-in meal at 1726 on 19 Feb. I waited in the queue all the way till 1756. I tried asking the manager(an Indian lady) where my order was, reasoning with her that orders from 1743 and before were already being served. The manager did not bother looking at the receipt and brushed me off, saying it's an automated system, and if I can't wait, she's more than willing to refund. Really bad response, worsened by what follows:
5 minutes later, another employee noticed that I've been there for quite some time and took a look at my receipt. She noticed something was very wrong and went back to the manager, who said she had already served the order since at 1730-something. Turns out they decided to serve dine-in orders in takeaway bags.

I don't think that's a standard practice? They could at least put a sign saying they are doing so. Hope the management can better train their staff to follow procedures properly, and at least try to understand the situation before dismissing or borderline threatening customers with a refund for something that's their fault to begin with.

The funny thing is that the aunties at the counter just asked me to buy food at other stalls even though I had paid in McDonald's. They said they were busy and no one tried to get my food ready. Then I requested to get refund and gave up the food. But they just refused and said how can I get a refund after I paid the money. (Totally wired logic)
Luckily, I am not in a hurry to do something today, and another auntie finally stood up, collected my food and beverage, and gave them to me (the food in my order is just ordinary ones, why took so long to prepare). But who wants to waste time on these tiny things, right?
Lesson: don't order at McDonald's in NTU if they already have a lot of orders to handle.

review_text:
Si Chuan Xiao Chu is a newly opened restaurant that offers authentic chinese dishes at very reasonable prices. Vegetable dishes are typically priced around 6-8, while meat dishes range from 8-12, making it a good option for casual dining with friends and family.

The flavours are impressive and taste quite authentic. One thing to note is that the dishes can be slightly oily, which is quite common for Sichuan cooking. If you prefer lighter flavours, it would be a good idea to request less oil when ordering, as the chef tends to be quite generous with it.

Overall, this is a promising addition to the quiet canteen.

name: Win Ee Chun
review_text:
Living in Hall 8 for 4 years, can9 was always my go-to spot for convenient meals.

Drinks stall aunties and uncle are super nice, and are easy to talk to. Yuan yang peng and milo peng are my favourites here.

Indian stall, if you can look past initial impressions, has pretty damn good curries. The butter chicken briyani here is a must try and a good deal for only 5 dollars.

Jiulixiang is OK if you know what to order - the hotpot is decent for sharing and value for money.

Caifan stall is pretty average, prices may fluctuate a bit but it's still decent. The better part is its tzi char, which is great. Queues are a bit longer, but the food is good - try the dry curry chicken, sheng mian, salted egg chicken, hotplate tofu and seaweed soup. Very good.

Mala stall is on the pricier side, but it's pretty good - try to go in the afternoons for the fried egg. The mala comes in two varieties too - Tom yum, and the regular. Both are good options.

The waffle stall opens in the evening, and a slightly less known item on the menu for Thursdays to Sundays is its mac n cheese and bolognese. The former especially is really good. Oh, they sell ice cream too.

review_text:
AFAIK the sole halal-only cafeteria in NTU campus and due to its central location, it's always crowded during lunch time (but less so during dinner hours). Some stalls often have super long queue, especially the Korean food and the economic rice.

The economic rice stall sells one unique item that is rarely found in other similar places, namely scallion pancake (Cong You Bing). This particular item is overwhelmingly popular among foreign students from Northern Chinese origin, who are accustomed with wheat-based staples instead of rice. It used to be even better and flakier, but the chef in charge of the pancake reportedly resigned in late 2025. This item is still there, just not as fantastic as it used to be.

Another unique stall in the cafeteria is the stir-fried yong tau fu stall. The item isn't particularly cheap compared to the rest of the stalls and even compared to the typical conventional yong tau fu.

Aside from the aforementioned economic rice stall, there's another one but seems to be of central China style. Most of the dishes are spicier and with healthy dose of ma la added. They also serve dumpling and liang pi, although I found their dumpling is inferior to others in the campus (for example, the one in South Spine Canteen). Maybe dumplings with thick skin isn't really my cup of tea.

The pho-and-banh mi stall is less popular but still pretty good. The chicken and beef pho are always nice to have in cool and damp rainy season. The zi char stall offers quite economical and sumptuous fried rice ($4), which is a godsend for many broke students in the campus.

response_from_owner_text:
Hi, thank you so much for your detailed feedback and for giving Each-a-Cup a great rating! We're glad to hear that you enjoyed our bubble tea, found our service efficient, and appreciated that the queue moves quickly.

Regarding the price of our milk tea, we understand that everyone has a different perception of value. We would just like to share that our milk tea is not simply regular tea with milk added. We use tea sourced from Taiwan, selected for its flavour and quality, and our drinks are prepared according to our established recipes to achieve the taste and consistency of a proper bubble tea.

We also strive to keep our prices reasonable while maintaining the quality of our ingredients and preparation. Compared with many bubble tea markets internationally, Singapore bubble tea remains relatively accessible, and we hope our customers can appreciate the balance between quality and price that we aim to provide.

We're also glad you enjoyed our non-milk teas and iced coffees. As our drinks can be customised, customers who prefer less sweetness can adjust the sugar level to their liking.

For payment, we currently accept cash and QR/PayNow payments. We understand that card payment would be more convenient for some customers, and we'll keep your feedback in mind as we review our payment options.

Thank you again for your support and thoughtful review. We hope to see you again soon for another cup!

Name: ANDES by ASTONS
name: Hailey
review_text:
I discovered this canteen through a friend's recommendation, and I must say, it never fails to impress me. Every visit is a pleasant surprise, and I always find myself wanting to return to try more dishes because the food is consistently excellent.

So far, I've tried several mains, and I highly recommend:
1. Thai Beef Noodle Soup - An authentic Thai-style herbal beef soup that reminds me of those at Golden Mile Complex. Add the chili for an extra kick!
2. Cajun Chicken Chop - Tender, flavorful chicken with a generous portion of creamy mashed potatoes, perfectly balanced with just the right amount of butter.
3. Nasi Lemak with Beef Rendang - A new favorite of mine! The rendang is rich and flavorful, and the beef is tender with a satisfying bite.

For desserts, I've enjoyed:
1. Churros - Crisp on the outside, soft inside, and delicious even on their own. They come with chocolate sauce and cinnamon sugar for dipping, making them even more irresistible.
2. Chatuchak Coconut Ice Cream - A refreshing treat that looks like an upscale version of our local chendol. A perfect way to end a meal!

I also love that they offer buddy meals and free-flow drinks, with options ranging from Teh Tarik and Milo to Coca-Cola and lemon tea.

Now, let's talk about the service--if I could give more than 5 stars, I would! The staff are incredibly warm and dedicated, and one person who stood out to me was Alya. Despite my brief interaction with her, it was clear she genuinely cares about customers. When I ordered the coconut ice cream for takeaway, she thoughtfully confirmed if I wanted it to-go, expressing concern that it might melt on the way home. She then went the extra mile to ensure it was well-packaged, and to my surprise, it barely melted even after 30+ minutes in Singapore's heat! Thanks to her, my family finally got to enjoy the ice cream I always rave about.

I've also noticed Alya's keen attention to detail--on another visit, she reheated a soup noodle dish because she felt it wasn't warm enough. These little gestures show her passion for service, and they truly make a difference. Alya, keep up the amazing work!

This canteen is a gem, and I highly recommend it for both the quality of food and the outstanding service. Looking forward to my next visit!

Name: The Soup Spoon Union
name: Jerry
review_text:
Halal Food. The food is good, and you can add $4 for a set that includes an additional soup and drink. The normal set costs $12.90. The staff mentioned that NTU has its own menu, which is different from other branches.

For the main course, I highly recommend the salmon (an additional $2). It is much meatier and more flavorful than at other places in NTU, but it tends to run out quickly. The sides (2 out of 3 from french fries, broccoli and corns) are served in large portions. For the soup, the mushroom soup is the safest option; tomato soup could be sour to some; pumpkin soup could be weird to some. The tea is freshly made on the day itself.

The staff are very friendly and patient, willing to answer any questions you have about choosing your meal or the free membership.

Regarding membership, you can collect points but cannot use vouchers because the prices are lower than at other branches.

Name: Pioneer Food Court
name: Yang
review_text:
Ice cream shop revived.

Teochew Braised Set for 2 pax($10)
Get their Kway. Comes with duck meat, tofu, egg, pig skin, pig intestine. The skin and intestine is good, quite clean.

Wanton mee($4)
Delicious. The char siew is soft and tender.

Hotstone Bibimbap($6)
Big sizzling bowl of bibimbap. Got chicken bulgogi, vege, bean sprout, carrot, radish and egg yolk over pearl rice and a spam of gochujang sauce.
Yummy and moderate spicy.
Serve with a bowl of savoury eggy soup with hint of pepper.

Mixed Rice($3)
Savoury cabbage, fried egg, stir-fry shabu meat then flood the rice in curry gravy. Simple and tasty.

Braised Duck rice and soup set ($6)
A pretty affordable meal at a decent price.
Duck rice is nice and flavoured but the rice grain kinda hard, with succulent duck meat down in savoury braised sauce. Add more chilli, shiok lah.
Radish pork rib soup, rich in flavour, strong in peppery taste, meat a bit little, soft radish.

Menya takashi Black King($8.80)
Big portion of noodles in rich and thick heavy Tonkotsu broth with char garlicky taste. Broth is great. Noodles will okay. Comes with marinated egg, bonito flake, pork belly char siu.
Dislike The pork belly char siu as is tough and hard to chew, stench of porky smell, not flavourful.
Topped up for Tako Ball($2.20)(3 pcs) not worth, very normal.

Pineapple Seafood Fried Rice($5.50)
Decent golden fried rice with distinct sweet pineapple taste in it, sprinkled with floss and cashew nuts. Comes with tender prawn.
Thai Honey Chicken($10)
Overly crispy chicken glaze in sweet honey but texture is kinda hard
Fried Crispy Beancurd Roll ($3)
Normal deep fried beancurd skin roll with sweet Thai chilli.
Shrimp Omelette ($6) - Sinfully oily but tasty but lacks crispness.
Kang Kong Garlic($6) - Normal savoury garlicky taste.

Mookata Set 1($20) consists of Chicken Thigh, Sliced Pork, Luncheon Meat, Fish Ball, Sausage, Crab Stick, Chinese Cabbages, Shiitake Mushroom, Golden Mushroom and Instant Noodles.
Meat was well marinated and tasty after cooking, hard to separate them for cooking as it stick together as one.
Soup was great too with all the essence from grill flowing down. Get salty overtime.

Sambal Fried Rice($5.50)(Thai Stall)
Unique fragrant Thai-ish replication of fiery red wok hei fried rice fried with chewy squid, fresh bouncey prawn, crunchy long bean, and eggs and garnished with fresh cut sliced onion. Its spiciness game get stronger after each mouthful or is it because I add chilli padi with soy sauce, but it does taste better with it.
It is nice but I believe it can be better too, just can't figure out what is lacking.
Expensive but worth it too.

review_text:
i have been a fan of encik tan for a long time now. in fact i was extremely excited when they decided to open a branch in NTU, i brought friends there for most of my lunches and many students like me enjoy encik tan - evident from the long snaking queues during peak hours that last for nearly 30 minutes each time.

however, my experience today (3 september, wednesday, 1pm) frustrated me deeply. i queued for approximately 20 minutes and ordered my usual set A (curry rice with chicken cutlet). i have known from patronising the stall for about 3 semesters now that the size of chicken cutlets has decreased over the last 1.5 years (thats okay/slightly sad, but the variation and shrinkflation is understandable).

BUT TODAY!! TODAY!! THE SIZE OF MY CHICKEN WAS THREE FINGERS THICC. AND DA CURRY. DONT GET ME STARTED. THE CURRY. WAS LIKE 1TBLSPN of curry mixed into 500ML OF WATER.

i was so upset. because what happened to the delicious thick gravy that i love from encik tan?? i walked away sadly, with my plate of food that i paid $5.30 for. in fact, when i ate it, the rice was clumpy and compressed -- nearly like a kueh. but i was already upset enough.

i am pretty certain that my experience would differ greatly if i ordered from a different branch! I understand that in NTU, the queues are long and the serving is pretty systematic and fast-paced. but that cannot excuse the strongly watered down gravy and rice quality. afterall, we are paying the same price for the same set.students deserve the same standards as any other branch, if not better. i truly hope Encik Tan NTU takes this feedback seriously and upholds the brand's reputation, instead of letting students walk away disappointed and disillusioned.

Name: Encik Tan
name: Ken Peh
review_text:
Read the low reviews here, think that it doesn't do Encik Tan justice and here's my review:

Food: They sell your usual Encik Tan fares like Curry Rice, Fishball Noodles, etc. Not the best you can get, but definitely okay for its price. $5 for a standard set of curry rice (Add $0.30 for takeaway). Top-up $1 for a lime juice, mid-sized cup, okay for an individual. Damage less than $7 per pax, though there are more expensive menus.

Service: Like fast-food, prompt and neat. Payment options include cash and credit card. Strangely, they don't accept PayNow or PayLah, despite being in a university campus, which is supposed to be chic and trendy.

Atmosphere: I've been to other Encik Tan branches which was really bad in terms of hygiene. This branch within NTU is air-conditioned and relatively clean.

Overall, a 3 to low 4-star, but definitely not those low star reviews you have seen here, which are emotionally driven in my opinion, not fair from a food seller view by Encik Tan.

review_text:
One pretty quaint lunch spot away from the more well-trafficked places in NTU campus, owned by a cheery middle aged couple. It's located in a concourse of the Experimental Medicine Building (third floor), accessible from the main North Spine complex from an overhead bridge.

Price is a bit more steep than in the cafeterias and they focus more on quality rather than portion size - perfect for dieting staffs and students. The menu is large - from pastries, sandwiches, cakes, wraps, cut fruits, coffee, and most importantly rice/pasta bowl with customizable topping (choices of meat, tofu, vegs). The pastries are served warm and fresh, and the bowl dishes' toppings are tasty. The coffee (espresso-based) is surprisingly pretty good and rather well-priced.

Can confirm sometimes there aren't enough seating during peak lunch time, albeit being situated inside a spacious concourse. More seating could be added so the customers can unwind.

Name: Mr Bean
name: Ken How
review_text:
I had a very disappointing experience with a male staff member (long hair) at Mr Bean today.

I was helping a colleague purchase an egg mayo toast and an almond soya drink. When I first informed that staff that I wanted an egg mayo toast, he did not respond. After a brief pause, he simply looked at me with an impatient expression, as if waiting for me to continue.

I then asked whether Mr Bean had an almond soya drink, as I was not familiar with the menu and was simply checking. Instead of responding politely, he reacted with a loud and abrupt "Huh?!", which came across as rude and dismissive. His tone made me feel embarrassed for asking a simple question.

I understand that staff may be busy during peak periods (which at that point of time, i was the only customer) but basic courtesy and professionalism should still be maintained. Customers should feel comfortable asking questions about the menu without being made to feel foolish. This interaction left a negative impression and fell short of the customer service standards I would expect.

Apparently, reading at the other reviews, I don't think I am the only one feeling this way about this individual. They should do something about it.

review_text: Tried the mocha, taste is not bad. My biggest gripe is the aircon seating area, which needs to stay open at least until afternoon tea break 430pm?
response_from_owner_text:
Hi Aaron,

Thank you for your kind words about our mocha--we're glad you enjoyed it!

We're sorry to hear about your experience with the air-conditioned seating area. Just to share, the aircon seating is co-managed by the store located within that space, and it is typically open until 5pm on weekdays. That said, we apologise for the lapse during your visit and any inconvenience caused.

We will definitely take note of this and work on improving the experience for our customers. We appreciate your feedback and hope to welcome you back again soon!

Name: Coffee Faculty
name: soheil haddad
review_text:
There used to be two excellent young men working there who always provided great service, but recently they hired a new staff member (a young woman) who unfortunately does not seem capable of managing even the basics properly. Beyond her poor work ethic, her attitude toward customers is shockingly rude. Imagine going in simply to enjoy a coffee and being met with the feeling that she would rather throw you out than serve you, what a shame for a place that once had such a welcoming atmosphere.
What makes it even worse is that this behavior cannot be justified by workload. It might be somewhat understandable if the cafe were constantly overcrowded and staff were overwhelmed, but that is not the case here. The shifts last less than four hours, and the number of customers rarely goes beyond twenty. With such manageable conditions, there is no excuse for such dismissive and unfriendly treatment.
Perhaps you could at least encourage her to be a little more motivated, and to start with something as simple as greeting customers with a friendly "hello."
response_from_owner_text:
Hi Soheil,

Thank you for taking the time to share your feedback, and we sincerely apologise for the late response. We're truly sorry to hear about your recent experience, and we appreciate you bringing this to our attention.

The staff member you mentioned is naturally a very quiet individual who takes some time to warm up to new environments and customers. That said, we fully understand that this should never affect the level of service our customers receive. We have since retrained her in customer service, and she has shown significant improvement in both her confidence and interactions with customers.

While she is still growing in her front-facing role, we want to share that she consistently prepares high-quality drinks and is an efficient, hardworking team member behind the counter. We are committed to supporting her so she can deliver equally well in customer interactions.

Thank you once again for your honest feedback -- it helps us do better. We hope you'll give us another chance to provide the warm and welcoming experience you've come to expect from us.

name: Yang
review_text:
Too much to write hit limit alr but will update pic.

New zi char Stall food is nice.

The zi char here move to canteen 1 already.

Brasied Sliced Fish with Soya Beancurd($9.80)
Tasted Same as boiled Sliced Fish. Just the vege change to tofu.

Green Curry with Rice Set($5.50)
BiG bowl of smooth and thick creamy coconutty green chicken curry. Savoury with a mild sweetness and isn't spicy at all. Long beans, tender chicken and firm potato with soft texture are found in it too.

Fish flavoured pork rice($4.50)
Chewy string shape pork stir-fry with onions, black fungus, bamboo shoot and spring onion in unique piquant vinegary mild spicy bean sauce mixture with various seasonings.

Sichuan Boiled Sliced Fish($9.50)
Big yummy smooth fish in spicy broth with a layer of oil. With various vege to be found. Spicy. Eat with rice.

Mee Soto($3.50)
Cheap and delicious. Add the black sambal foe xtra shiokness.

Phat Thai($5)
Barely pass. Still a savoury tangy dish. Normal.

Breakfast Set($2)
Super soft light toast with little Kaya Butter spread.
Half Boiled Egg - Egg yolk is 3/4 done
Coffee/Tea - coffee with condensed milk. moderate, milkiness normal, just a bit too watery.
Meh... Average.

Mapo Tofu Rice($4)
Had the basic but still can be improve. Soft silken tofu stir-fry with leek, bean sauce, chilli and peppercorn, etc.
Piping Hot, Mild spicy, Subtle fragrance, Colour Authetic, Numbness Mild, Crispness Lack.
The taste is light and comfortable but not traditional enough. Seem like it adjusted to local taste here but anyway, it still a great dish.

XLB($4.50) - Yummy, juicy succulent meat
Dumplings in red chilli oil($4.30) - Nope... Thick skin & sauce is salty
Normal dumpling are great ($4)

Tom Yum fried rice from xuji cuisine($3)
Got the smell but no tom yum taste.
Fried rice is normal. Lack quality.

Ayam Penyat($5) - Okay to try, chicken skin crispy, meat is a bit dry

Waffle($1.30) plain - Crispy outer, chewy inner with a nice fragrance

Mala - Expensive and not worth it, not fragrant and spicyness isn't there

Roasted Chicken + Char Siew Rice($5)
Generous portion. Roasted chicken taste old and normal. Plasticky Char siew is better. Okay to try 1 time.

Fish & Chips($4.80)

review_text:

Unfortunately, the experience left a very bad aftertaste -- and not because of the food.

I was in a rush for class, so I politely asked the barista if he could make my coffee faster. I asked a few more times, but he refused, and when I requested a refund, he said it would take half an hour.

review_text:
The correct address for North Hill Food Court is 60 Nanyang Crescent, Blk 21A, #02-02 Singapore 636957, in case anyone is lost with Google Maps. It is located below Banyan Hall Block 21A. Alternatively, there is a staircase from below if walking from the bus stop. Food is generally okay but be prepared to be paying at least SGD4 and above for a decent meal (SGD3.50 for a normal plate of chicken rice, though my opinion is not worth).

My personal favourite is mala (alternative if Hot Hideout is closed or too crowded) and Chinese Zi Char from 2nd stall from the left (some friends called it "Malay Stall" although it isn't halal as the stall was originally located at the right end where the original Malay stall was). As for halal food, there was an indian stall open last semester but not sure if it is still operating. Hence, for halal options I would recommend either the Indian restaurant below at level 1 or to take a walk to Hall 11's malay stall/waffle stall (both sell good stuff) and Tamarind Canteen's Indian stall.

name: MNG
review_text:
Sichuan Mei Shi is one of the busiest stall within this canteen. The other being mixed veg rice.

A self order system with a big selection of menu available. Since it is loosely translated into English, it can be confusing.

Boiled chicken (what it is called here) is essentially Kou Shui Ji was excellent. The chicken was served on top of cold cucumber and the accompanying sauce was appetizing.

Mapo tofu is another Sichuan dish. Though the numbness (Ma) is toned down, the bean sauce was fragrant and went well with steamed rice.

Double cooked pork aka Hui Guo Rou was disappointing as the pork belly were overcooked. The onion was surprisingly sweet.

For a canteen stall, this is beyond my expectations, both in taste and value.

name: Niyu Yuqian
review_text:
As a Hall 11 resident for 2 years I think I can give a good review of this canteen.

Best stall is the caifan stall. Always long queue. If you are short like me I suggest you to take a pic with phone over your head if you want to see the dishes on top. Make your decision quick or else the uncle will give you stress.

Japanese stall is my second favourite, sometimes long queue. I recommend the ramen and curry rice.

For supper delights, I recommend waffles stall. Buy with the ice cream it's super nice. However, it may be closed on some days without prior notice.

For Sichuan delights it's good once in a while. Portions are big so bring your friends along if you want to try this. It works like zi char in coffee shops so you order few dishes and eat with rice. It also sells ala carte dishes like fried rice. Again, portion too big for me. Good if you have big appetite.

Noodles stall is quite ordinary. No exceptionally outstanding dishes to recommend. It's good if you want healthier options with soup.

Muslim stall have special dish on different days of the week. I like the mee soto. Didn't try the rest.

For drinks stall, I recommend yuanyang and teh (not coffee) for caffeine . For cold drinks there are plenty of cans/bottles/packets to choose from. Their breakfast sets are also nice and cheaper than other canteens nearby. Their pows and lor Mai gai is also good. They also sell chicken essence cos this school can be quite a pressure cooker.

There's another stall which sell fruit juice and milkshake. I love the banana milkshake. Quite nice but this stall is not for you to buy your regular fruits. You can get cheaper and bigger portions with more choices at other canteens.

I had a very unpleasant experience at this Starbucks today.
The female staff member at the counter was clearly impatient from the start. When I didn't catch her question about cup size, she rudely pointed at the menu and rolled her eyes, which felt completely unnecessary and disrespectful.

Later, when she asked "take it away?" (which she said too quickly for me to understand), I asked her to repeat, and she stared at me again before slowing down. Her attitude was cold and condescending throughout the interaction.

To make it easier, I had even prepared a screenshot showing exactly what I wanted -- drink type, cup size, sugar level -- and specifically asked for just one pump of syrup, but the drink I received did not match my request at all.

There was no queue behind me, no pressure or rush. Still, I was treated like I was causing a problem just for not catching her words the first time.

I always try to be respectful when ordering, and I understand that service work can be tiring -- but basic courtesy is the minimum. I felt very uncomfortable and disappointed. I will not return to this store.

review_text: Very bad experience. I went here because it was near my house and that during the holidays it would not be crowded (and it was not at all through out the day), but was shocked to see a rude and demanding service staff and especially, manager. I sat at one of the larger tables because I wanted to do my work and because there were only 3 people in the entire store. It was not even 2 minutes until I was being pressured by the manager to buy something, and even when I told him I would soon, just at my own time and pace, he was apparently not happy with my answer nor my freedom of choosing to get anything. It was not even 10 minutes into my visit, where I was just setting up my books and had my bag across me in another seat and had even ordered a drink which was part of a membership privilege, in the empty store when I got approached again by the manager and he rudely demanded, and I quote 'Today is a Sunday, so there will be a large crowd, so if you don't plan on getting a drink and wasting space to do your work, can you please move elsewhere' Shocked by such behavior, I even told him I had already ordered a drink and informed him that I would move if I saw the crowds getting bigger. Throughout the entire time, I was being glared at by him and what was worse was when I went to get my drink, and in front of my face was he telling his service staff to not be afraid of 'people like me' who 'pay nothing for drinks' and to ask me to leave and go elsewhere if i wanted to study. Honestly, things got even worse fro there, but I cannot even start to describe how disgusted I actually am by the service of this outlet. Forget about being a starbucks member for years, I was not even treated like a regular customer would even be. Everyone working at this outlet, especially the manager should be ashamed of the way they treat people. I was never in my life made to feel so uncomfortable in a cafe/restaurant.  I will go off to another outlet, but never in my life come back to this one, no matter how near it is to me.

name: Aqil said
review_text:
It is my belief that common decency and mutual respect are crucial for the workings of any business. That being said, hall 14's drink stall, the only stall I can eat at due to halal concerns and price, remains a sore point in my visits.
During the day, the auntie running the stall, whose primary language is Mandarin, replies to me and my room mate in English with sarcasm every time we order something. Unfortunately, both of us do not speak Mandarin. If we dare enquire further, she raises her voice at us. The same cannot be said for patrons who communicate with her in Mandarin, who are treated more decently, being called affectionate names and the like. During the night, the couple running the store can only speak in mandarin, forcing my room mate and I to play a game of charades or use the calculator as a means of getting numbers across. I understand for a fact that Foodgle is unconcerned with the running of their stalls overall. Stall owners are merely rotated around different halls when complaints arise from my observations of NTU's different food courts.
I'm not writing this to get Foodgle to do anything knowing full well they won't. I am writing this to let others know that I understand their pain. Not being able to speak the same language seems to bar us all from the enjoyment of luxuries such as coffee and tea without bearing some insults. The hall 2 drinks stall owner used to shout at non-mandarin speakers too. Several other horror stories are commonplace in Foodgle foodcourts. Until such a time comes when we are liberated from the tedium of living, studying and striving to better ourselves in university, this will never change.

review_text:
I rarely review food court stalls due to their generic food that can be found elsewhere.

BUT why I am reviewing this is due to the fact there is an amazing store here that I feel I need to share with everyone and the fact this place is pretty isolated.

The Dry Ban Mian Store is just simply put AMAZING. I tried their Dry Ramen and there no words describing how good it is. It is simply restaurant standards and the tanginess of the noodles and flavouring in their sauce just made me wordless at first bite. I also added abit of chilli on my first trying and for my second trying I added more to make my ramen spicy. But you can perfectly eat it without chilli as well.

The soup version is just ok as well but not as nice as the dry.

Considering the affordable price (refer to picture), this stall is a must vist.

There is also a Japanese store. (Refer to image) The food is pretty ex for a food court. $6 and above minimally but it's not bad. No wow factor but decent.

Western food is halal. Decent cream spaghetti but abit tough chicken chop.

The food court opened at 11am daily and closes at 8pm.

There's parking nearby. Or you can always just take public transport.

Food court is non-airconditioned.

name: lontongstroong
review_text:
Located a tad bit out of the way from the well-trafficked areas of NTU's North Spine and I've only known this place rather recently. Surprisingly popular among some students and staffs - there is always crowds around lunch time, perhaps the 10% discount of all items on sale for them is one of the main draws.

Discount aside, the offerings are actually pretty good given the price, albeit the Japanese and Japanese-inspired noodle dishes' portion is somewhat smaller than average for most people. The coffee is one of the very bests in NTU and very competitively priced ($3 for long black/espresso after discount). Don't expect the variety like real speciality coffee place like let's say Venture Drive, but they are know what they are doing - the coffee I've had was chocolaty, a bit velvety, and came with right 'body' and thickness.

Due to its popularity, the indoor space is very crowded in lunch time, but the outdoor dining space (next to a rooftop garden) is almost always empty. Some shading (even patio table with umbrella) would do, especially in hot weather.

Name: Connect 71 Cafe (C71)
name: Angela Cheah
review_text:
Rating this purely for the chocolate cake sold here. DISCLAIMER I SAY FIRST EVERYTHING ELSE HERE IS GOOD, I JUST WANT TO REVIEW THE CHOCOLATE CAKE. Let's start off with looks cos it was what intrigued me and my friend to want to buy it. We agreed that it looked like the cake from the Mr Bean TV animated series and the cake from Mathilda that Miss Trunchbull made Bruce eat. It sounds like we're glazing it's looks but that was rly what sold us to buying it. Was only $4 dollars and was splitting it two ways so each oni paid $2 so not the worst as well. Now here is where it went downhill and sent us into the five stages of grief.

Act 1, DENIAL: First taste right off the bat, did not rly like it but still tried to convince myself that it's decent.
Act 2, ANGER: The more we ate it, the more we realised how unexcusably bland it was. The texture screamed industrial cleaning sponge that's never met moisture, the irony. And we were in disbelief and anger that we let our glutton appetite be fooled by the cake's looks and price. It's like we could use this to scrub a toilet and the toilet would've probably apologised for the inconvenience.
Act 3, BARGAINING: As we ate the cake, our anger turned into a struggle to find meaning of this cake. Saying how even cheap/ affordable cake stores like polar and primadeli can do a better job, cos their chocolate cakes actually have the taste of cocoa which doesn't seem like a hard requirement. Calling it a chocolate cake might have been a big slap to the face of cocoa farmers worldwide.
Act 4, DEPRESSION: Reaching the end of the cake, we started to wallow in our thoughts and in our seats. Bloated from the amount of water we needed to drink to mask the weird aftertaste in our mouths after every bite. Saying, I miss how my mouth tasted before eating this.
Act 5, ACCEPTANCE: Finally finishing the cake, we left the place, with Phlegmy throats induced due to the dryness and weird texture of the cake. Accepting what we had eaten and there's nothing we can do about it. So moving forward, we will not be ordering this cake anymore. BUT, we will still be coming back to eat the other food like the mains and the drinks, those are super solid 4/5. Staff are also rly friendly 5/5. Just this cake was rly bad sorry.

name: caleb lau
review_text:
Food here was of a decent quality. The noodles were springy and condiments complement each other well. Each bowl, be it the don or ramen, has been well thought through, from the ingredients and the distinct flavour each one gives.

Maze soba ($7), the cheapest ramen on the menu, is a dish that cannot go wrong. The spice is mild and suitable for most palates, and the fermented bean taste in the minced pork is not too strong, suitable for my tastebud. Giving fresh chopped spring onions and soft boiled egg, though simple, but when combined give the bowl multiple layers.

The taro latte ($4.50) is one of numerous flavoured lattes offered here, both iced or hot. Though it does not look particularly aesthetic, the flavour of the taro matched with the milk makes all the difference. The small bits of taro make the drink more special and add texture to the smooth taste.

Overall the vibe of the place is chill, as reflected in the background music played here as well. Will recommend to come post lunch crowd instead of during the peak hour as tables are limited. What is good is that the tables are spaced out, giving more privacy to each group of customers and more pleasing to the eyes. The isolated location of the cafe on one hand makes it harder to access and known to others, but on the other it's that very fact that makes the place unique in identity to NTU itself. Furthermore, NTU/NIE staff enjoy 10% discount, and students enjoy $1 their drink if bought with a meal. Though not a steal due to its price and not student-friendly, but it is good for occasions in small groups.

Name: Paik's Bibim
name: Benson
review_text:
Paik Bibim is easily one of the hidden gems in NTU. I've visited multiple times and the quality has never disappointed. The food is always fresh, flavourful, and served in generous portions that leave you feeling satisfied.

The signature bibimbap is excellent, with perfectly balanced flavours and ingredients that work beautifully together. Every dish tastes like it was prepared with care rather than rushed out of the kitchen. The prices are also very reasonable, especially considering the quality and portion size.

Beyond the food, the staff are warm, polite, and genuinely welcoming. The restaurant is clean, comfortable, and has a pleasant atmosphere that makes you want to stay a little longer.

It's not easy to find a place that consistently delivers great food, good service, and excellent value, but Paik Bibim manages to do all three. Highly recommended for anyone craving authentic Korean food in NTU. Looking forward to many more visits!

Name: Paik's Bibim
name: KY Pang
review_text:
One of the best Korean dining experiences I've had in NTU. The food at Paik Bibim is consistently delicious, with generous portions and great value for money. The bibimbap is packed with fresh ingredients, the sauces are flavourful without being overpowering, and every dish arrives hot and well-prepared.

What really stands out is the consistency and service. Even during busy meal hours, the staff remain friendly, efficient, and attentive. The restaurant is clean, well-maintained, and has a welcoming atmosphere that makes it a great place for both students and visitors.

It's rare to find a place that combines quality, portion size, taste, and affordability so well. Paik Bibim has become one of my go-to spots in NTU, and I highly recommend it to anyone looking for authentic and satisfying Korean food.

Will definitely keep coming back!

Other than that, choose between savoury or sweet and sour sauces to complete your bowl. Oh, and their scrambled egg is top notch, extremely creamy, soft and fluffy if you're an egg fan.

I dined in, and the experience was OK. Not too cold or hot, sometimes I guess one or two flies will make their way in due to the lack of a strong air-conditioning curtain? So one star off.

Service is excellent, staff is friendly, attentive and quick.

This canteen excels in long term forecasting inflation. They priced their dishes so far into the future, you need at least two decades for other canteens to keep up.
The same combination of dishes for mixed vegetable rice will cost $6.40 in other canteens. Over here, it'll cost a whopping $7.80. It's not like a famous tire company gave them a star either (if they did then pls take it away, it's trash tier quality).
I believe part of their rationale behind the premium pricing is the Italian inspiration behind their food. In particular, their rice was hard enough to compete with those in a risotto.

Name: Food Court 4
name: lontongstroong
review_text:
This is one of the smaller cafeteria in the NTU campus, smack in between one of its student dorms. Mostly advertises itself serving authentic Northern Chinese home-cooked cuisine and street food. There's not many stalls inside the cafeteria - only a cai png, jianbing guozi (savory crepe), drink stations, and interestingly, pizza stall.

I believe it's the only place where you can get authentic jianbing in NTU campus, or even perhaps in the entire West. The jianbing isn't particularly the cheapest thing (above $4.5 per serving), but it comes with pretty large portion. Big enough for heavy breakfast (I can see why it's popular among college kids) or even lunch. Soft in the outside, crispy in the middle, and rather generous filling of meat and cabbage in the center. Beware it comes PIPING hot with somewhat inadequate and flimsy paper packaging!

review_text: Extremely frustrating service because they were severely understaffed on soft launch weekend, mismanagement fro. HQ and poor staff training. We received our food an hour later and after customers who came after us; They finished and left even before our order came to us. They missed the order sequence and so order was completely skipped/forgotten; most likely they just confirmed that order was completed when it was not. We had to explicitly remind them to check on our order. Don't know why they decided to do a soft launch and have only one server (and probably only one chef) managing such a large crowd over a weekend. And mind you this was a festive weekend, and I am sure all restaurants would be preparing for increased activity and business, but no, it was the complete opposite here. In fact they put the Closed sign just an hour into their service, way before their close time, and turned away many guests even though the restaurant was half empty. I won't be recommending any of our NTU community members nor will I entertain any guest that come my way to this place. restaurant.

Name: Man Le Chinese Restaurant
name: guocamoleyi
review_text:
Visited on 26 July 2026 at around 7:30pm.

Extremely poor service with an unfriendly attitude.

The short-haired waitress who served us accidentally dropped a spoon, so I politely requested a replacement as it might have become dirty. She replaced it, but did so very reluctantly.

We were also unable to find any pork dishes on the menu, so we asked if any were available. Instead of pointing them out, she simply repeated the name of the dish several times. We eventually had to explicitly ask where it was listed on the menu before she showed us.

Finally, when she asked if we would like any drinks, we declined because we had brought our own water bottles. She then repeated twice that outside drinks were not allowed, which was confusing as we were only drinking plain water from our own bottles.

Overall, the service was dismissive, unhelpful, and left us feeling unwelcome. As this is a newly opened restaurant, I unfortunately cannot recommend visiting based on our experience. The service was practically non-existent.

review_text:

Fried Rice with Prawn Paste Chicken($4.50)
Tasty. Delicious.

Mala Prawn Paste Pao Fan($6)
Good spicy pao fan.

Prawn Mee(L)($3.30)
Generous amount of prawn, vege and fishcake. Savoury prawny soup.

Nasi Padang($5.10)

Basmatic Rice, Sambal Goreng Tahu Tempe, Stir Fry Kambing, Sambal Long Bean, acar timun.

Mala Maggi goreng dry pot($12.30)

Overall, its a tastisfying bowl of Mala pot. Price is quite reasonable too. Option were many too. Nice.

Bak Chor Mee($2.50(S)/$3.30(L))
Not only the Price is cheap, the noodles were great too. Savoury springy noodles with the right amount of vinegary taste, topped with soft & juicy mushroom and a load of meaty minced meat. Get the large bowl for extra ingredients.

Chicken Chop($3.80) with Spaghetti($4.80)
When you on budget but want to eat western too. All you need is $5 and can fill your stomach full.
Standard chicken chop with the meat on the tougher & dryer side with slightly char skin, covered with the black pepper sauce, it makes it quite decent. Comes with pre-mix mashed potato(I guess) and garden green salad.
As for spaghetti, its al dente and drenched with a choice of sauce from two option, which are
Chicken Bolognese - Tomato based with strong herb taste & minced chicken. Surprisely nice.
Cream of Mushroom - Your safe option.

Grilled fish with Spaghetti($5)
Soft tender silky fish with lightly grilled skin, flood with sauce of your choice, comes with garden salad.

review_text:
The bak chor mee stall sells bak chor mee, lor mee, fish ball noodles and prawn noodles. The queue will be long at peak hours (1130-1pm).

If you visited the stall quite often, the uncle will remember what you like to order. The uncle is nice but sometimes he will be bad tempered when the queue is too long.

To facilitate the order, and make the order flexible, you can tell uncle these:
1. small portion, or big potion (add noodles and/or ingredients, can specify what ingredient to add also). The more you add the higher the price but very worth.
2. Type of noodles: mee pok, mee kia, mi fen, huang mian, lao shu fen, cu mi fen (can point if you are not sure the name)
3. Spicy or not spciy
4. Hidden menu: dried version or wet version.

During sem break, the bak chua mee may change to other type of food like fried kway teow, hokkien mee and wa tan hor, with minumum $4.

PS: no more wa tan hor, but fried kuey teow and hokkien mee are available during school semester, and you don't need to join the queue for them

Name: Food Court @ NIE
name: Fomsy Porter
review_text:
A delightful canteen with multiple food offerings priced cheaply. Meals here are wallet-friendly (<$4) and sometimes when they have deals like using paylah for purchases, you can get a dirt cheap meal.

It is no wonder that students, staff and the public like to come here to eat. I have even seen army officers dining here.

If you love Chinese food, go for the shop called 'Noodles', which serves local delights like bakchormee and lor mee, and'Fish soup', which serves fares like ban Mian. I wouldn't recommend the cai fan store, unless there is no queue. Most of the stall owners are friendly, with the exception of the western stall.

name: Jeremy Tay
review_text:
Highly negative experience at chinese cai fan stall regarding the use of CDC vouchers.

On more than one occasion, the right-most staff member when facing the stall would get passive aggressive when I asked if I could use CDC vouchers to pay, asking me if he could reject the method, rounding up the price to make it match the CDC vouchers' sum exactly instead of letting me top up the remaining cost via PayNow, and questioning why I wanted to save that bit of cash.

It is embarrassing for the customer to have to deal with this in front of other customers, as if I shouldn't eat at the stall if I'm "poor".

If you don't want to accept CDC vouchers, don't put the sign there.

It's a shame because the food is good, but not good and cheap enough for people to repeatedly get humiliated in public.
